Empirical Research Plan for Evaluating Chile’s “P-900” School‐Improvement Program
================================================================================

1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------
• Method: Fuzzy Regression‐Discontinuity-in-Differences (RD-DD).

Why RD?  
– Assignment was based on an explicit cut-off in the 1988 fourth-grade SIMCE score, applied separately within each of the 13 regions.  
– Schools could not ex-post manipulate their 1988 scores, so the running variable is as‐good‐as-random around the threshold.

Why “fuzzy”?  
– A second screening stage excluded some below-cut-off schools (small, remote, managerial problems) and possibly allowed a few above-cut-off schools in, so treatment probability, rather than treatment status, jumps at the threshold.

Why add “Differences”?  
– Mean reversion is a first-order concern when selection is based on a low prior score. Taking changes (1988→1990 or 1988→1992) or stacking a pre-period (1984→1988) differences nets out the mechanical bounce-back and isolates the discontinuous change attributable to the program.

Baseline estimating equation (local linear):  

ΔScore_ir ≡ (Score_1990 – Score_1988)_ir  
  = α + τ·Treated_ir + f_–(Score88_ir – c_r) + f_+(Score88_ir – c_r) + ε_ir ,

estimated within a symmetric bandwidth h around each regional cut-off c_r, with treatment instrumented by BelowCutoff_ir to deliver a fuzzy RD.  

2. Treatment and Control
------------------------
Treatment variable  
 Treated_ir = 1 if school i in region r actually received the P-900 package starting 1990; 0 otherwise.

Running variable  
 X_ir = 1988 combined SIMCE score (language + math) expressed in SDs or raw points.

Cut-off  
 c_r = region-specific threshold chosen by the Ministry in 1989. Define distance to cut-off:  
  Running_ir = X_ir – c_r (negative values are “eligible”).

Instrument  
 BelowCutoff_ir = 1{Running_ir < 0}.

Control (counterfactual)  
 Schools with Running_ir just ≥ 0 (within the chosen bandwidth) that were not treated.

Timing  
 Treatment begins January 1990. Outcomes observed in 1990 (short-run) and 1992 (medium-run). Pre-program trends can be checked with 1984 and 1988 scores.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcome trends at the cut-off.  
 Plausible: 1988 scores were produced two years before the program and are not manipulable later.

A2. Exclusion: No other policy or shock jumps at the same regional threshold.  
 Reasonable: P-900 was the only nationally announced intervention tied to the 1988 score ranking.

A3. Monotonicity (fuzzy RD).  
 All else equal, being below the cut-off weakly increases the probability of treatment—violated only by forced exclusions.

A4. Parallel pre-trends (for RD-DD).  
 Within a narrow window, untreated potential score changes from 1988 to 1990/92 should be smooth in Running_ir. We can test this using 1984→1988 gains.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers in the narrow RD window).  
 Possibility of resource displacement across nearby schools is limited; we can probe for spillovers by adding the share of neighboring treated schools.

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-----------------------------------------
T1. Selective post-cut-off exclusions (small, rural schools).  
 – Test and control for discontinuities in enrollment, rural dummy, SES index.  
 – Implement trimmed samples (e.g., drop schools <15 pupils), or estimate separate RDs for urban/rural subsamples.

T2. Mean reversion bias.  
 – Main design uses gain scores.  
 – Include a placebo RD using 1984→1988 change; τ̂ should be ≈ 0 pre-program.

T3. Spillovers to control schools within the same commune.  
 – Add commune fixed effects and/or drop communes where >50 % of schools are treated.  
 – Re-estimate on geographically isolated schools.

5. R Code Outline
-----------------
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)
library(fixest)     # fast OLS/IV with fixed effects
library(rdrobust)   # RD inference

# ---- 1. Load data ----
dat <- fread("chile_school_panel.csv")  # object: one obs per school-year

# ---- 2. Keep relevant years and reshape ----
dat_w <- dcast(dat, school_id + region + urban + ses90 + enrol88 ~ year,
               value.var = c("score_math", "score_lang"))
# create combined scores
dat_w[, score88 := (score_math_1988 + score_lang_1988)/2]
dat_w[, score90 := (score_math_1990 + score_lang_1990)/2]
dat_w[, score92 := (score_math_1992 + score_lang_1992)/2]
dat_w[, score84 := (score_math_1984 + score_lang_1984)/2]

# ---- 3. Running variable and instrument ----
cutoffs <- fread("regional_cutoffs_1988.csv")   # region, c_r
dat_w <- merge(dat_w, cutoffs, by = "region")
dat_w[, running := score88 - cutoff]            # distance to threshold
dat_w[, below := as.integer(running < 0)]

# ---- 4. Outcome variables ----
dat_w[, dscore90 := score90 - score88]          # 88→90 gain
dat_w[, dscore92 := score92 - score88]

# ---- 5. Main fuzzy RD (88–90 gain) ----
# narrow ±15 raw‐score points (~1 SD) as baseline bandwidth
bw <- 15
sample <- dat_w[abs(running) <= bw]

# local linear IV with separate slopes
est <- feols(dscore90 ~ treat | 0 |
             running:below + running:!below | 
             0,            # no FE
             iv = ~ below,
             data = sample)
summary(est, cluster = ~region)   # cluster at region level

# ---- 6. rdrobust version (automatic bandwidth) ----
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = sample$dscore90,
                   x = sample$running,
                   c = 0,
                   fuzzy = sample$treat)        # treat is actual program take-up
print(rd_out)

# ---- 7. Pre-trend placebo (84–88) ----
sample[, dscore88 := score88 - score84]
placebo <- feols(dscore88 ~ treat | 0 |
                 running:below + running:!below,
                 iv = ~ below,
                 data = sample)
summary(placebo, cluster = ~region)

# ---- 8. Covariate continuity check ----
cov_test <- feols(enrol88 ~ below + running, data = dat_w[abs(running)<=bw])
summary(cov_test)
```

6. Expected Results
-------------------
Economic priors and contemporaneous evidence from textbook/teacher training programs suggest modest but positive gains. I expect:

• τ̂ ≈ 0.10–0.15 SD increase in fourth-grade combined score by 1990 (one year of exposure).  
• Additional 0.05–0.10 SD by 1992 if effects accumulate.  
• Conventional before/after comparisons (ignoring RD) likely exaggerate effects to ≈ 0.25–0.30 SD because of mean reversion.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
------------------------------------------
C1. Precise, predetermined running variable …… 1  
C2. No manipulation at the threshold ………… 1  
C3. Continuity of baseline covariates ………… 0.5  
C4. No other discontinuous shocks at cut-off … 1  
C5. Limited spillovers within bandwidth ……… 0.5  

Total ≈ 4/5 => research design is credibly causal but warrants robustness checks on covariates and spillovers.
